discovery_method._tooling_constraints_2026_09_04: TWO HARD LIMITS discovered this run, both of which cost budget if rediscovered. (1) web_fetch enforces a PROVENANCE SET: it will only retrieve a URL that literally appeared in a user message, a previous web_fetch result, or a WebSearch result. You CANNOT construct a URL — not from this config, not by adding ?page=N. Templated URLs in the 'venues' list above must therefore be surfaced by a WebSearch first (search the page title, e.g. "USENIX Security '26 technical sessions"), THEN fetched. (2) The built-in browser pane requires per-site approval, which a scheduled non-interactive run cannot grant: navigation to raid2026.org and dblp.org both returned 'denied or failed'. So the DBLP-TOC channel and any JS-rendered accepted-papers page are UNAVAILABLE in scheduled runs — they need an interactive session. CONSEQUENCE for large venues: the USENIX '26 technical-sessions page is paginated and one fetch yields only ~54 of ~400 titles with no way to page forward. Substitute a domain-restricted WebSearch (allowed_domains usenix.org) using the scope keywords; that is the workable exhaustive-ish channel for big programs.

domain_restricted_topical_sweep.why: The only channel that finds correctly-scoped papers whose titles share no vocabulary with the keyword list — see _keyword_blind_spot_2026_09_06. Produced the Bilingual Problems (USENIX Sec '23) catch on its first use, and NatiSand (RAID '23) + the 'Extending a Hand to Attackers' exclusion on its second (2026-09-07). THIRD USE, 2026-09-08: produced 'Too Much of a Good Thing: (In-)Security of Mandatory Security Software for Financial Services in South Korea' (USENIX Sec '25) — a top-4 paper, in the backfill window, invisible to every keyword channel because its title contains none of the config vocabulary. That is now THREE consecutive runs in which this channel, and only this channel, produced a correctly-scoped backfill miss. TWO LESSONS ON QUERY WORDING: (a) 'inter-process communication privilege boundary application' returned almost nothing but US patents — abstract OS-systems phrasing pulls the patent corpus, not security venues, so keep the wording APPLICATION-SHAPED ('desktop application', 'web content', 'renderer', 'add-on') rather than OS-primitive-shaped ('IPC', 'privilege boundary'). (b) The two productive queries this run both named a CONCRETE ARCHITECTURE ('untrusted web content renderer', 'local HTTP server desktop agent'). Prefer architecture nouns over mechanism nouns. The rotation list has been extended to ten queries and 'not_yet_used' emptied; treat the list as a ring buffer and consult 'queries_used_so_far' to pick the least-recently-used two or three each run. FOURTH USE, 2026-09-09: ALL THREE remaining unused queries were fired and the channel produced NOTHING new — the first null result in four runs. The results were dominated by pre-2020 classics (Protecting Browsers from Extension Vulnerabilities NDSS'10, JSand ACSAC'12, The Effectiveness of Application Permissions WebApps'11) and, for two of the three queries, by US PATENTS and PL-theory papers. This CONFIRMS AND SHARPENS the 2026-09-08 wording lesson: 'attack surface measurement' and 'foreign function interface' are METRIC/MECHANISM nouns and they pull the patent + programming-languages corpus, exactly as 'inter-process communication privilege boundary' did. The rotation list is now fully consumed once. WHEN REFILLING IT, write ARCHITECTURE-SHAPED queries in the style of the two that actually worked ('sandbox escape desktop application untrusted web content renderer', 'local HTTP server desktop agent web page privileged API security study') — name a concrete component ('preload script', 'auto-updater', 'custom protocol handler', 'deep link', 'notification bridge', 'packaged app bundle') rather than an abstract property. Suggested next-round queries: 'custom URL scheme handler desktop application attack', 'auto-update mechanism desktop client integrity study', 'deep link handling native application web origin', 'markdown renderer desktop note-taking application injection', 'chat client link preview server-side request'. One null run is NOT yet evidence of backfill convergence — it is one data point, and it was spent on the three weakest-worded queries in the buffer. FIFTH USE, 2026-09-10: NULL for a second consecutive run, and it re-confirms the wording rule a third time. The five queries fired were the config's own suggested refills plus two of my own. 'custom URL scheme handler desktop application attack' returned almost entirely US PATENTS - 'URL scheme handler' reads as a MECHANISM noun to the search index despite sounding architectural. 'markdown renderer desktop note-taking application injection' returned scattered unrelated USENIX/ACM papers with no topical cluster at all. 'auto-update mechanism desktop client integrity study' returned exactly one target-venue paper and it was ALREADY EXCLUDED (When Updates Backfire, USENIX Sec'26). 'deep link handling ...' returned only mobile/Android deep-link work (all pre-2020 or already excluded). 'preload script contextBridge renderer main process desktop app study' returned Inspectron - already in_scope - which is a POSITIVE control: the channel does surface the right cluster when one exists, so the nulls are informative rather than tooling failures. SHARPENED RULE: a query is architecture-shaped only if the named component is one a DEVELOPER WOULD NAME IN AN APP'S SOURCE (preload script, auto-updater, link preview, drag-and-drop handler), not one an OS or spec would name (URL scheme, IPC, FFI, deep link).
